data.one_liner: Config-based scraper for web pages and APIs using chainable parsers and transforms.
data.what_it_does: Extracts data from web pages and APIs using simple key/value configurations and chained parsers. It supports over 15 built-in parsers including HTML, CSS selectors, JSONPath, tables, and response headers.
use_when: You need to scrape web pages or APIs using configuration-driven patterns.
You want to extract structured data from HTML tables or JSON endpoints without writing boilerplate parsing logic.
avoid_when: You need a full headless browser solution to execute complex client-side JavaScript interactions.
You are scraping heavily authenticated applications requiring complex session management.
strengths: Over 15 built-in parsers with support for elements, attributes, text, JSON paths, and headers.
Automatic browser-like request headers and user-agent generation.
weaknesses: Relies on static HTML fetching and cannot execute JavaScript-heavy Single Page Applications natively.
Config-based approach may become difficult to maintain for extremely complex scraping workflows.
